BS Prem: solve for the flat vol that reproduces each ticker's own 50Δ contract's actual market price (Black-Scholes-Merton, using this page's risk-free rate and each ticker's own trailing dividend yield — NOT OCM's raw reported IV, which we verified is not self-consistent with its own mark price here), then apply that flat vol across all strikes at that expiry. The 50Δ gap is ~0% by construction; other buckets show how much the market's actual skew/smile premium deviates from a flat-vol assumption. Green = market cheaper than flat-vol BS; red = market richer. Outlined cell = largest |gap| in that row. The separate "IV" column is OCM's own reported field, shown for reference — it can diverge materially from the BS-solved vol (see the 50Δ column vs. the BS Prem's implied 0%-gap baseline).

BS Prem: solve for the flat vol that reproduces each ticker's own 50Δ contract's actual market price (Black-Scholes-Merton, using this page's risk-free rate and each ticker's own trailing dividend yield — NOT OCM's raw reported IV, which we verified is not self-consistent with its own mark price here), then apply that flat vol across all strikes at that expiry. The 50Δ gap is ~0% by construction; other buckets show how much the market's actual skew/smile premium deviates from a flat-vol assumption. Green = market cheaper than flat-vol BS; red = market richer. Outlined cell = largest |gap| in that row. The separate "IV" column is OCM's own reported field, shown for reference — it can diverge materially from the BS-solved vol (see the 50Δ column vs. the BS Prem's implied 0%-gap baseline).

BS Prem: solve for the flat vol that reproduces each ticker's own 50Δ contract's actual market price (Black-Scholes-Merton, using this page's risk-free rate and each ticker's own trailing dividend yield — NOT OCM's raw reported IV, which we verified is not self-consistent with its own mark price here), then apply that flat vol across all strikes at that expiry. The 50Δ gap is ~0% by construction; other buckets show how much the market's actual skew/smile premium deviates from a flat-vol assumption. Green = market cheaper than flat-vol BS; red = market richer. Outlined cell = largest |gap| in that row. The separate "IV" column is OCM's own reported field, shown for reference — it can diverge materially from the BS-solved vol (see the 50Δ column vs. the BS Prem's implied 0%-gap baseline).

BS Prem: solve for the flat vol that reproduces each ticker's own 50Δ contract's actual market price (Black-Scholes-Merton, using this page's risk-free rate and each ticker's own trailing dividend yield — NOT OCM's raw reported IV, which we verified is not self-consistent with its own mark price here), then apply that flat vol across all strikes at that expiry. The 50Δ gap is ~0% by construction; other buckets show how much the market's actual skew/smile premium deviates from a flat-vol assumption. Green = market cheaper than flat-vol BS; red = market richer. Outlined cell = largest |gap| in that row. The separate "IV" column is OCM's own reported field, shown for reference — it can diverge materially from the BS-solved vol (see the 50Δ column vs. the BS Prem's implied 0%-gap baseline).

BS Prem: solve for the flat vol that reproduces each ticker's own 50Δ contract's actual market price (Black-Scholes-Merton, using this page's risk-free rate and each ticker's own trailing dividend yield — NOT OCM's raw reported IV, which we verified is not self-consistent with its own mark price here), then apply that flat vol across all strikes at that expiry. The 50Δ gap is ~0% by construction; other buckets show how much the market's actual skew/smile premium deviates from a flat-vol assumption. Green = market cheaper than flat-vol BS; red = market richer. Outlined cell = largest |gap| in that row. The separate "IV" column is OCM's own reported field, shown for reference — it can diverge materially from the BS-solved vol (see the 50Δ column vs. the BS Prem's implied 0%-gap baseline).

Every listed (buyΔ, sellΔ) bull call-spread combination across all 9 tickers and their listed expiries, where sellΔ > 0.3 × buyΔ (keeps the short leg from being too deep-OTM/thin to trust its quote), the sell leg's premium is between 30% and 70% of the buy leg's premium (keeps the short leg from collecting negligible credit or eating too much of the long leg's cost to be a real spread trade), AND both legs pass a liquidity check measured in implied-vol space: bid > 0, and (IV at ask − IV at bid) ≤ 10% of the leg's own mid-IV — a default that favors genuinely liquid, tightly-quoted contracts over marginal ones (e.g. on an 18%-IV name that's only ≈1.8pp of allowed IV spread). A $ spread that looks huge on a cheap far-OTM LEAPS contract can still be a tight, genuinely-tradeable IV band, while a similar $ spread on a broken/unquoted contract is a huge IV band (BKNG Jan28 strikes with $0 bids or flat $20 asks showed 19-39pp IV spreads on ~35% IV — correctly rejected either way). Discount % = (Mkt Debit − BS Debit) ÷ Mkt Debit — the flat-vol Black-Scholes debit uses each expiry's own 50Δ-calibrated vol (same methodology as the main screener tab). Positive/green = paying less than flat-vol fair value (skew working in your favor); negative/red = paying a premium over it. Sorted by Discount % ascending. Click any column header to re-sort; click a ticker to open its detail page.

Every listed (buyΔ, sellΔ) bull call-spread combination across all 7 tickers and their listed expiries, where sellΔ > 0.3 × buyΔ (keeps the short leg from being too deep-OTM/thin to trust its quote), the sell leg's premium is between 30% and 70% of the buy leg's premium (keeps the short leg from collecting negligible credit or eating too much of the long leg's cost to be a real spread trade), AND both legs pass a liquidity check measured in implied-vol space: bid > 0, and (IV at ask − IV at bid) ≤ 10% of the leg's own mid-IV — a default that favors genuinely liquid, tightly-quoted contracts over marginal ones (e.g. on an 18%-IV name that's only ≈1.8pp of allowed IV spread). A $ spread that looks huge on a cheap far-OTM LEAPS contract can still be a tight, genuinely-tradeable IV band, while a similar $ spread on a broken/unquoted contract is a huge IV band (BKNG Jan28 strikes with $0 bids or flat $20 asks showed 19-39pp IV spreads on ~35% IV — correctly rejected either way). Discount % = (Mkt Debit − BS Debit) ÷ Mkt Debit — the flat-vol Black-Scholes debit uses each expiry's own 50Δ-calibrated vol (same methodology as the main screener tab). Positive/green = paying less than flat-vol fair value (skew working in your favor); negative/red = paying a premium over it. Sorted by Discount % ascending. Click any column header to re-sort; click a ticker to open its detail page.
